body: As far as I know this is just not done for performance reasons, because rescanning all dirs for new translation files on every request would be quite expensive. Perhaps someone else has a better explanation though.

It's not that expensive if you only scan the translation dirs.

I think it's just that no-one has implemented it yet.
Thank you guys! I would like to have a warning about such cases in the documentation. Working in the dev environment, I guess the cache is cleared.
@schmittjoh so even in dev translations require the cache to be cleared for them to update? or only when new files are added?
Only adding new translation files requires a cache clear. But it is still an inconvenience, and if it can be fixed it'd be great.
It was my understanding that the cache was cleared on every dev request, is it not?

No that would make things very slow. The cache (or most of it anyway) is checked for freshness in dev mode, so that the parts that need to be modified are rebuilt, while in production these checks are skipped for performance, and the cache is assumed to be always fresh.
@Seldaek AH! ok now i understand, that makes much more sense.

This would be partially fixed by #391 which is still planned for 2.1 as I understand.
The problem is that the cache is compiled with existing resources and since the translation component can always find a fallback, it won't look for something new. Listing translation directories as resources to watch for changes in the cache instead of listing files. Then only when adding a new translation directory would this problem appear.

issue.title: [FrameworkBundle] Monitor added/removed translations files in dev
